raw_evidence_cards.document_title: A Comprehensive Survey on Graph Reduction: Sparsification, Coarsening, and Condensation
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: A comprehensive survey on graph reduction methods (sparsification, coarsening, and condensation), establishing a unified framework for simplifying large graphs while preserving essential properties. It systematically reviews technical details of graph reduction algorithms and their applications across diverse scenarios.
overlaps: Covers graph summarization/reduction as a method for compressing large graphs into smaller graphs, which overlaps with GSAERU's graph summarization component
Discusses graph coarsening methods that produce reduced graphs with fewer nodes, conceptually similar to GSAERU's compression of dynamic sequential graphs into fixed-size new graphs
Mentions combining graph reduction with GNNs for scalability, which is related to GSAERU's use of graph summarization to enable GNN training
differences: Does not specifically address the combination of graph summarization with a graph autoencoder for training node representations via reconstruction error
Does not address feeding compressed graph representations into a recurrent neural network (RNN) to learn temporal features and dependencies
Does not model dynamic sequential graphs as a sequence of snapshots at each time step
Focuses on graph reduction for scalability and performance preservation in static graph settings, not on temporal/sequential graph representation learning

raw_evidence_cards.document_title: Scaling R-GCN Training with Graph Summarization
raw_evidence_cards.main_contribution: Scaling R-GCN Training with Graph Summarization proposes using graph summarization techniques to compress graphs before training a Relational Graph Convolutional Network, reducing memory requirements and computational overhead, then transferring weights back to the original graph for inference.
overlaps: Uses graph summarization to compress the graph for GNN (R-GCN) training
Aims to reduce memory and computational overhead during GNN training
differences: Training is performed on a single machine (GPU memory constraint), not in a distributed leader-worker mode
No leader node performing graph partitioning via an edge-based graph flow partition algorithm
No worker nodes performing mini-batch training based on graph summarization
No attention layer used to return training results to a leader
No synchronous model update across multiple computing nodes

sources.title: Scaling R-GCN Training with Graph Summarization
sources.quote: we experiment with the use of graph summarization techniques to compress the graph and hence reduce the amount of memory needed. After training the R-GCN on the graph summary, we transfer the weights back to the original graph and attempt to perform inference on it.
